chapter_name: Chapter 13: Short Writing Skills (Diary Entry and Notices)
learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will master the precise formats, tones, and concise language required for drafting official notices and expressive personal diary entries.]
warm_up_hook: 📝 Whether you are making a massive announcement to the whole school or whispering a secret to a blank page, short writing skills are all about maximum impact with minimum words! Let's master the art of brevity! ✂️

lesson_modules.module_title: 📌 The Notice Board: Formal and Factual
lesson_modules.teaching_content: A Notice is a formal announcement. It MUST be placed inside a box. It has a strict format: Name of Institution, the word 'NOTICE', Date, Heading, Body, and Signature. It must answer the 5 Ws: What, When, Where, Who, and Whom to contact.
examples_or_templates: Tone: Formal, passive voice preferred, absolutely no first-person pronouns (I, me, my).

lesson_modules.teaching_content: A Diary Entry is a personal record of an event or feeling. It includes the Day, Date, and Time at the top left. The tone is informal, emotional, and always written in the first person ('I').
examples_or_templates:
Format: 
Monday, 14th October 2024
9:00 PM

Dear Diary,
Today was the most thrilling day...

lesson_modules.teaching_content: The biggest difference is the audience. A notice is for the public; it must be clear, polite, and objective. A diary is for yourself; it can be passionate, subjective, and use emotive adjectives.
examples_or_templates: Notice: 'A gold watch was found in the playground.' (Objective)
Diary: 'I was absolutely devastated when I realized I lost my grandfather's watch!' (Subjective)

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which of the following is NOT required in the format of a Notice?
options: A box drawn around the text

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ What is the most appropriate pronoun to use when writing a Diary Entry?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Draft the body (just the 5 Ws) of a Notice informing students about an upcoming Inter-House Debate Competition.
subjective_practice.hint: Include: Event name (What), Date/Time (When), Auditorium (Where), Students of classes 8-10 (Who), and submit names to English teacher (Whom to contact).

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Write the first two lines of a Diary Entry about a day you surprisingly won a medal in a race you didn't train for.
subjective_practice.hint: Start with the Day, Date, and Time. Then express your sheer shock and excitement in the opening sentence.

activity_or_assignment.title: 🎭 The Two-Faced Writer
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Imagine your school is organizing a trip to a theme park. First, write a formal 50-word Notice as the Head Boy/Girl announcing the trip. Second, write a 100-word Diary Entry as a student expressing how excited you are to go on the rollercoasters with your friends.

chapter_summary: ⭐ Notices are formal, boxed, under 50 words, and must clearly answer the 5 Ws (What, When, Where, Who, Whom).
⭐ Diary Entries are highly personal, written in the first person ('I'), and express deep feelings and reflections.
⭐ Never use casual language in a Notice, and avoid sounding robotic or overly formal in a Diary Entry.
